requirements.requirement: Run a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status confirms all three rabbit@node1/2/3 nodes present as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes after join_cluster; reconfirmed identically after each node's restart.

requirements.requirement: Serve AMQP over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A dedicated CA (ca-key.pem/ca-cert.pem) was generated on node1 and used to sign per-node server certs and a client cert (openssl verify OK). rabbitmq.conf on each node sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile pointing at this CA's material; ss -tlnp confirms only 5671/ssl is listening (no plaintext 5672) on all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Accept only client connections presenting a certificate issued by that CA
requirements.summary: ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true are configured on all nodes. Direct TLS tests show: a CA-issued client cert succeeds (Verify return code 0); no client cert triggers a 'certificate required' fatal alert; a cert from a different, untrusted CA triggers a 'Bad Certificate' fatal alert (confirmed both via openssl s_client output and rabbit@node1 log). End-to-end AMQPS publish/consume with the CA-issued client cert succeeded against all three nodes both before and after the restart cycle.

requirements.requirement: Keep the management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: management.tcp.ip binds 15672 to each node's private cluster IP only (not 0.0.0.0), and iptables rules on each node allow 15672 only from the three cluster node IPs followed by a catch-all DROP, persisted via netfilter-persistent. Reachability from within the cluster was verified (401 on bad creds, i.e. connection succeeds). However, no test was captured showing a connection attempt from an IP outside the three-node allowlist was actually blocked/dropped, so the negative case (exclusion of non-cluster sources) rests on configuration inspection rather than an observed blocked connection.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cluster/data/firewall/TLS state
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id bfd05127... and healthy cluster/queue state captured; reboot issued; connection loss observed across several poll attempts; post-reboot boot_id bf8463cc... (changed) confirmed; rabbitmq-server active, cluster shows 3/3 running, iptables 15672 rules intact, and queue data (tls_test_q) persisted post-restart. Consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (bfd05127... -> bf8463cc...).

requirements.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cluster/data/firewall/TLS state
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id cf34dc87... captured; reboot issued with observed connection loss; post-reboot boot_id f499ebdc... confirmed changed; rabbitmq-server active, cluster_status shows 3/3 running, iptables 15672 rules intact. Consistent with fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cluster/data/firewall/TLS state
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id 63f96994... captured; reboot issued with observed connection loss; post-reboot boot_id 1af46fc6... confirmed changed; rabbitmq-server active, cluster_status shows 3/3 running, iptables 15672 rules intact. Consistent with fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check. End-to-end AMQPS messaging and TLS client-cert enforcement re-verified against all nodes after the full restart cycle.

overall_summary: The executor built a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster with AMQP served exclusively over TLS on 5671, backed by a dedicated cluster CA, and enforced mutual TLS (verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert) such that only CA-issued client certificates are accepted — directly demonstrated via positive (valid cert) and negative (no cert, foreign-CA cert) TLS handshake tests, plus end-to-end AMQPS pub/sub. The management interface is bound to each node's private IP and firewalled via iptables/netfilter-persistent to the three cluster IPs with a catch-all DROP; reachability from within the cluster was verified, though no test captured a blocked connection from outside the allowlist. The mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol was executed for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity changes, connection-loss evidence during the reboot, and confirmed recovery of cluster membership, firewall rules, and TLS/AMQP functionality afterward, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. One unnecessary, unreverted mutation (an abandoned SSH key/authorized_keys setup) was found during hygiene review.
limitations: No captured evidence of an actual blocked connection attempt to the management API from an IP outside the three-node cluster allowlist; the exclusion relies on iptables rule inspection and interface binding rather than an observed negative test.
No cleanup command was captured for the SSH key material written to node1's ~/.ssh directory during the abandoned SSH-based file-distribution attempt, so its final state is unconfirmed.
Restart-window observations rely on repeated connection-reset/timeout polling rather than a continuous log capture, so the exact disruption boundary is inferred rather than directly logged.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map cleanly to task outcomes: package installs, CA/cert generation, TLS config, cluster join, iptables rules (persisted), user management, and the restart protocol. The temporary HTTP file server used to distribute certs to node2/node3 (cmd-37cd1e1adaf04ab9) was bounded and explicitly torn down afterward (cmd-1c9dc408e96d4d19), which is good practice. One unnecessary mutation was identified: cmd-ff791179a4964a92 wrote an SSH private key to ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 and appended a public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on node1 in an attempt to set up SSH-based file distribution to node2/node3; this attempt failed (return_code 255, sshd inactive on peers) and the executor pivoted to the HTTP-server approach instead. No subsequent command was captured removing the written SSH key material, so this residue (low sensitivity, but an added credential/authorized_keys entry) was not shown to be cleaned up.
